You sell cakes on weekends. Hobby or business? CRA has a test, and it changes your taxes.
CRA's definition: a business is an activity you intend to carry on for profit, with evidence to back that intention.
Evidence means facts: prices, records, marketing, a plan, a real chance of profit.
If it's just a personal pastime, there's no business income. And no business loss either.
Our Manitoba baker earns sixty thousand at a day job. Cakes bring in eight thousand; ingredients cost three. Five thousand profit.
As a business, that's about two thousand and eighty in tax and CPP.
But a business can also lose. First year: sales two thousand, costs thirty-five hundred. Minus fifteen hundred.
That loss lowers the salary income: about four sixty back. A hobby gets nothing.
